title: Omni-fMRI: A Universal Atlas-Free fMRI Foundation Model
claim: Our method achieves the best score across a wide range of benchmarks, outperforming competing models on nearly every task.
layout: Single radial bar chart around central mascot, clockwise, color-coded legend bottom-right
description: A circular radial bar chart surrounds a cartoon pink brain with a cute face, viewed through a black magnifying glass. Ten benchmark labels (NKI-Age, NKI-Edu., BHRC-Sex, HCP-Tasks, Emo-Sad, Emo-Happy, ABCD-Sex, ADNI-AD, ADNI-MCI, PPMI) sit on a ring around the brain, each with a curved underline. Outward from each label, a cluster of three or four bars shows performance with numeric values printed on them. Colors identify methods: red/pink for Omni-fMRI, orange for Omni-fMRI (LP), green for NeuroSTORM, and blue for SwiFT. A legend in the lower right maps colors to names. The Omni-fMRI bars are generally the longest in each cluster. The eye goes first to the brain mascot, then outward along the colorful bars.
caption: Omni-fMRI reaches the best performance across a diverse array of resting-state and task-based fMRI benchmarks.
abstract: Self-supervised fMRI foundation models have shown promising transfer performance, yet most rely on predefined region-level parcellations that discard fine-grained voxel information and introduce atlas-dependent biases. We propose Omni-fMRI, an atlas-free foundation model that operates directly on voxel-level signals. To enable scalable pretraining on 49,497 fMRI sessions across nine datasets, Omni-fMRI introduces a dynamic patching mechanism that substantially reduces computational cost while preserving informative spatial structure. To support reproducibility and fair comparison, we establish a comprehensive benchmark suite spanning 11 datasets and a diverse set of resting-state and task-based fMRI tasks. Experimental results demonstrate that Omni-fMRI consistently outperforms existing foundation models, providing a scalable and reproducible framework for atlas-free brain representation learning. Code and logs are available.
